target: Part: the flowering stems (stem, PO:0009047) carry almost no leaves, but the basal leaves are present and 2-pinnate.
fix: 'mostly leafless', 'nearly leafless' and 'leafless' describe the stem or scape they belong to. That stem carries few or no leaves; never annotate 'leaf absent' for the taxon.
reason: Ranunculus multifidus has a rosette of 2-pinnate basal leaves and flowering stems with few leaves.

target: No absence of the inflorescence. The text says where the tendrils sit: they are never on the inflorescence (tendril, e.g. branch tendril PO:0025364, absent from the inflorescence PO:0009049).
fix: 'never borne on <part>' and 'not borne on <part>' tell where something else is placed. They are never the absence of <part>; the absence (if any) belongs to the subject of the sentence (here the tendrils).
reason: Rhoicissus has cymes, described as ± condensed. Only the tendrils are said not to be on them.

target: Part: the flowering stalk (stem, PO:0009047) has no leaves; the basal leaves are present, with smooth margins.
fix: '<stalk/scape> ... and leafless' means that stalk carries no leaves (same rule as X01051/X01077).
reason: Camassia has basal leaves and a leafless flowering scape.

target: Sex: there are no staminate (male) spikelets; the pistillate spikelets (spikelet, PO:0009051) are present and nearly sessile.
fix: 'no staminate <part>' and 'no pistillate <part>' are absences of that sex form only. Keep the sex qualifier (staminate flower PO:0025600 / pistillate flower PO:0025599), or drop the absence; never 'spikelet absent'.
reason: Carex abdita has pistillate spikes that are sessile or nearly so. Only the male spikes are missing.

target: rosette (PO:0025615) absent (PATO:0000462): the plant has no basal rosette; the stem leaves are present.
fix: 'no tuft of basal leaves', 'no basal rosette' and 'without a rosette' mean the rosette (PO:0025615) is absent. They never mean the leaf is absent.
reason: Centaurium pulchellum has stem leaves, which are greyish green. It just lacks the basal rosette seen in C. erythraea.

target: Sex: the pistillate flowers (PO:0025599) have no petals; the staminate flowers (PO:0025600) have narrow white petals.
fix: In unisexual taxa, 'no petals' next to a description of petals usually belongs to one sex. Keep the absence on the flower of that sex (the sentence or paragraph naming male or female flowers), never on the taxon.
reason: In Croton, the male flowers have petals and the female flowers lack them.

target: Leaf type: there are no basal leaves; the stem leaves (cauline leaf, PO:0000013) are present and pale green beneath.
fix: 'no basal leaves' is the absence of basal leaves only (same rule as X01066). Keep the qualifier, or drop the absence if there is no class.
reason: Doellingeria umbellata has leafy stems and lacks a basal rosette when it flowers.

target: Part: the flowering stems (stem, PO:0009047) carry no leaves; the basal rosette leaves are present (oblong or oblanceolate).
fix: '<part> are leafless' means that part carries no leaves (same rule as X01051).
reason: Erophila verna is a rosette annual with leafless scapes.

target: Floret type: there are no disk florets (disk flower, PO:0025332); the ray florets (ray flower, PO:0025331) are present and yellow.
fix: 'no disk florets' and 'no ray florets' are the absence of that kind of floret: use disk flower PO:0025332 or ray flower PO:0025331, never flower PO:0009046.
reason: Hieracium heads are made only of ligulate (ray-like) florets.

target: Flower form: the cleistogamous flowers (closed, self-pollinating flowers) have no petals; the open (chasmogamous) flowers have petals with purple veins.
fix: 'cleistogamous flowers without <part>' covers only the cleistogamous flowers. Keep that qualifier, or drop the absence; never record it for the taxon.
reason: Violets have two flower forms: open flowers with petals and closed flowers without them.

target: Location: the upper glume (PO:0006004) has no awn; the lemma awn (PO:0006032) is present and geniculate.
fix: '<part> awnless' and '<part> muticous' mean that part has no awn (awn absent on that part). They never mean every awn of the taxon is absent.
reason: In Andropogon, the glumes are awnless and the upper lemma carries a geniculate awn.

target: Leaf type: some leaves (submerged or phyllode-like leaves) have no floating blade; the floating leaves have a lamina (PO:0020039) with a strongly cordate base.
fix: 'without a floating blade' and 'without a blade' in aquatic plants refer to one kind of leaf (submerged, juvenile, phyllode). Keep the leaf kind, or drop the absence (same rule as X01066).
reason: Aponogeton has submerged and floating leaves; the cordate base belongs to the floating blades.

target: Leaf type: some leaves have no blade (they are phyllode-like); the bladed leaves have a lamina (PO:0020039) with an obtuse tip.
fix: 'leaves ... (sometimes) without blade' in a description that also describes blades is the absence for one kind of leaf (same rule as X01091).
reason: Aponogeton species often have leaves both with and without a blade.

target: Part: the flowering stem (stem, PO:0009047) has no leaves for most of its length; the basal leaves are present and sword-shaped.
fix: 'leafless for most of its length' is said of a stem or scape: that stem carries few leaves (same rule as X01051).
reason: Aristea has sword-shaped basal leaves and a flowering stem that is mostly bare.

target: Floret type: the ray florets (ray flower, PO:0025331) are sterile and have no style; the disk florets have styles. The pappus annotation is not about the style.
fix: In Asteraceae, 'rays sterile, without styles' is the absence of the style in ray flowers (PO:0025331) only. Keep the floret type on the absence.
reason: In Aspilia the ray florets are neuter and the disk florets are fertile. The pappus cupule is a different part and only came up because of the pairing.

target: Floret type: there are no female florets (pistillate flower, PO:0025599); the bisexual florets are present and white.
fix: 'female florets absent' and 'male flowers absent' are the absence of that sex form (PO:0025599 / PO:0025600), never flower PO:0009046.
reason: The heads have only bisexual florets, and those are described as white.

target: Sex: the staminate flowers (PO:0025600) have no ovary; the ovary of the bisexual or female flowers is globose.
fix: 'ovary absent' (often written 'ovary absent or rudimentary') sits in the paragraph on male flowers. Keep the absence on the staminate flower, never on the taxon.
reason: The ovary is described as globose, so the absence must belong to the male flowers.

target: staminode (PO:0009077) absent (PATO:0000462); the stamens are present, with flattened filaments.
fix: 'staminodes absent' and 'staminodia absent' mean the staminode (PO:0009077) is absent. They are never the absence of the stamen; match the word itself, not its stem.
reason: Chrysophyllum lacks staminodes; the stamens are described.

target: Stage or season: the leaves fall in dry periods (deciduous, PATO:0001730), so the stems are often leafless. Record deciduous, not absent.
fix: 'frequently leafless', 'often leafless' and 'leafless when flowering' together with 'deciduous' describe a seasonal state. Record the leaf as deciduous; never record an absence.
reason: Cissus quadrangularis has small leaves that drop early, leaving the green stems bare.

target: portion of secretory tissue (gland, PO:0005656) absent (PATO:0000462) at the base of the petal (PO:0009032); the petal itself is present and puberulous.
fix: 'without glands at the base' means the part being described has no glands there (same rule as X01069). It is never the absence of that part.
reason: Clutia petals can have glands at the base or lack them; here the glands are missing, not the petals.

target: No absence of the fruit: the fruit (PO:0009001) has no apical peg (beak) at its tip. There is no PO class for the peg, so make no absence statement, or record the fruit apex as not beaked.
fix: 'apical peg absent', 'beak absent' and 'stipe absent' are absences of a small outgrowth of the fruit. Never give the absence to the fruit itself.
reason: The fruit is described (lepidote body and wings). Only the peg at the tip is missing.

target: Floret type: the outer female florets (pistillate flower, PO:0025599) have no corolla; the disk florets have a dry membranous corolla.
fix: In Asteraceae, 'female florets ... without a corolla' covers only those florets. Keep the floret type on the absence (same rule as X01094).
reason: In Cotula the marginal female florets often lack a corolla, while the disk florets have one.

target: No annotation from 'Fruits not seen'. The woolly description probably belongs to another taxon or is of the ovary, so check where it comes from.
fix: '<part> not seen' means not observed, not absent (same rule as X01054). If the same part is also described, check whether the description belongs to another taxon merged into the record.
reason: 'Not seen' says the fruit is missing from the specimens, not from the plant. The woolly fruit text has another source.

target: aril (PO:0009090) absent (PATO:0000462); the seed is present and mottled with black.
fix: 'aril absent', 'caruncle absent' and 'strophiole absent' are the absence of that seed appendage, never of the seed.
reason: The seed is described as densely mottled; only the aril is missing.

target: No absence of the stipule (PO:0020041): it is not spiny ('not aculeate') and not accrescent (not growing larger with age). The 'accrescent' annotation must also be negated.
fix: 'not aculeate' means not prickly or spiny: the part has no prickles, it is not absent. In 'not X nor Y', the negation covers both X and Y.
reason: The stipules exist; the sentence negates two qualities. The present statement is also wrong because it lost its negation.

target: No absence from 'style not seen'. The triangular papillose appendages are tips of the style branches, which were seen in other florets or specimens.
fix: '<part> not seen' means not observed (same rule as X01054); never record it as an absence.
reason: 'Not seen' is about the material examined. The style appendages are described elsewhere.

target: Stem type: there is no leafy above-ground stem (the plant has no visible main stem); the basal leaves are present and arcuate (curved).
fix: 'without leafy stems' means the plant has no leafy aerial stem (same rule as X01076). It is never the absence of leaves.
reason: The leaves are said to be mostly basal, which goes with a plant that has no leafy stem.

target: Bract kind: there are no primary bracts (the large, leaf-like bracts at the base of the inflorescence); the ordinary bracts (PO:0009055) are present and deciduous.
fix: '<qualifier> bracts not present' (primary, involucral, floral bracts) is the absence of that kind of bract only. Keep the qualifier or drop the absence (same rule as X01066).
reason: Some Hymenodictyon species have enlarged leaf-like bracts that this species lacks, while other bracts are present.

target: Spikelet: the pedicelled (or homogamous) spikelets are muticous (no awn); the sessile spikelet's lemma awn (PO:0006032) is present and puberulous.
fix: 'muticous' (awnless) applies to the spikelet or glume being described in that sentence. In grasses with paired spikelets, keep it on that spikelet; never record 'awn absent' for the taxon.
reason: In Hyparrhenia, the sessile spikelets have hairy awns and the pedicelled spikelets have none.

target: Leaf type: the stem has no sheathing cauline leaves (cauline leaf, PO:0000013); the basal leaf is present and linear.
fix: 'without sheathing leaves', 'without cauline leaves' and 'without stem leaves' are the absence of leaves on the stem only (same rule as X01066).
reason: Moraea callista has a linear basal leaf and a stem with no sheathing leaves.
